Cluster sequences using Mixed Markov Models

Source: R/mmm.R
cluster_mmm.Rd

cluster_mmm() clusters sequences by fitting a mixture of first-order Markov chains and returns the fitted net_mmm object: the same fit, with the same arguments, as build_mmm(). The fit holds each sequence's subgroup and posterior probabilities, the mixing proportions, the information criteria and the subgroups' transition matrices.

Pass the fit to build_network() to get one network per subgroup, or use cluster_network(..., cluster_by = "mmm") to fit and build the networks in one call. build_mmm() explains how to read the fit and what to check before trusting it.

Usage

cluster_mmm(
  data,
  k = 2L,
  n_starts = 50L,
  max_iter = 200L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  smooth = 0.01,
  seed = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  covariate_effect = c("em", "posthoc"),
  estimator = c("auto", "firth", "multinom", "chisq"),
  cluster_by = "mmm",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

The sequences: a data frame with one row per sequence and one column per position, a netobject or bare cograph_network built from sequences, or a tna model (whose stored states are decoded to their labels). Columns take the same roles as in build_network(): an id or a covariate is not a position, and the columns set aside are named in a message and kept as metadata. Association networks (cor, pcor, glasso, ising, mgm) hold variables, not sequences, and raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

k

The number of subgroups (mixture components), a whole number of at least 2. Default 2.

n_starts

How many starting configurations to try, a positive whole number. More starts make it likelier that the best local maximum is found. Default 50.

max_iter

The most EM iterations a start may run, a positive whole number. Default 200.

tol

The convergence tolerance: EM stops when the log-likelihood changes by less than this between iterations (with covariate_effect = "em", also when its relative change does). A finite positive number; default 1e-6.

smooth

A pseudo-count added to every transition count before the matrices are estimated, so a transition unseen in a subgroup gets a small probability instead of zero. A finite non-negative number; default 0.01.

seed

An integer that makes the random starts reproducible. Default NULL. The session's own random stream is left as it was.

covariates

Variables describing each sequence (such as a course or a grade), given as a column name, a character vector of names, a one-sided formula or a data frame, as in build_clusters(). For a netobject, names are looked up in its metadata first, so a typical call is build_mmm(net, k = 3, covariates = "session_label"). How they enter the model is set by covariate_effect. Default NULL.

covariate_effect

How covariates enter the model. "em" (default) makes the mixing proportions depend on them during EM, so they shape the subgroups found and add (k - 1) * p parameters for p covariate columns; rows with a missing covariate are dropped first, with a warning. "posthoc" fits a plain mixture on every sequence and relates the covariates to the subgroups only afterwards, with a multinomial logit, so neither their values nor their missingness change the subgroups. Ignored without covariates.

estimator

How the after-fit multinomial logit is estimated; it never affects the EM. "auto" (default) uses Firth's penalised likelihood (brglm2::brmultinom(), finite under separation) when a cell of the subgroup-by-covariate table has fewer than 5 sequences, and nnet::multinom() otherwise. "firth" and "multinom" force one of them ("multinom" warns about separation risk), and "chisq" runs descriptive tests instead of a logit. build_clusters() has the details. Ignored without covariates.

cluster_by

The clustering family. Only "mmm" (the default) is accepted; it is there so cluster_mmm() and cluster_network() share one call shape. Any other value raises an error that points to cluster_network().

...

Not used; any extra argument raises an error.

Value

A net_mmm object, exactly as build_mmm() returns it: print(), summary() and plot() read it, build_network() turns it into a netobject_group with one network per subgroup, and cluster_diagnostics() gives the classification and, for sequences built from long data with actor/session, session_ids() gives each sequence's subgroup. build_mmm() lists its fields. For HTNA input, the actor partition is kept and restored when the fit is turned into networks with build_network() or as_htna().

Details

cluster_mmm() takes the arguments of build_mmm() plus cluster_by, so its call has the same shape as cluster_network().

See also

build_mmm(), build_network(), and cluster_network() for fitting and building the per-cluster networks in one call.

Examples

seqs <- data.frame(V1 = sample(c("A","B","C"), 30, TRUE),
                   V2 = sample(c("A","B","C"), 30, TRUE))
fit <- cluster_mmm(seqs, k = 2, n_starts = 1, max_iter = 10, seed = 1)
fit
#> Mixed Markov Model
#>   Sequences: 30  |  Clusters: 2  |  States: 3
#>   ICs: LL = -64.101  |  BIC = 186.022  |  AIC = 162.201  |  ICL = 188.063
#>   Quality: AvePP = 0.967  |  Entropy = 0.197  |  Class.Err = 3.3%
#>   Status: did not converge in 10 iterations
#> 
#>   Cluster  N           Mix%   AvePP
#>   1        28 (93.3%)  91.6%  0.973
#>   2        2 ( 6.7%)    8.4%  0.888
cluster_diagnostics(fit)
#> Cluster Diagnostics (mmm) [k = 2]
#>   Sequences: 30  |  Clusters: 2  |  States: 3
#>   Quality: AvePP = 0.967  |  Entropy = 0.197  |  Class.Err = 3.3%
#>   ICs: LL = -64.101  |  BIC = 186.022  |  AIC = 162.201  |  ICL = 188.063
#> 
#>   Cluster  N           Mix%   AvePP  Class.Err%
#>   1        28 (93.3%)  91.6%  0.973   2.7%
#>   2        2 ( 6.7%)    8.4%  0.888  11.2%
# \donttest{
# Visualise with sequence_plot
seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 40, TRUE),
  V2 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 40, TRUE),
  V3 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 40, TRUE)
)
fit <- cluster_mmm(seqs, k = 2)
sequence_plot(fit, type = "index")

# }
